Incorporating Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) signals into the assessment:

- Banks broadly eased standards for household credit (residential real estate, credit card, auto, and other consumer loans) and reduced minimum required credit scores, with large banks also easing on HELOCs and GSE-eligible mortgages—supportive for credit availability.
- Large banks eased standards for investment-grade firms, but some banks tightened C&I lending policies and foreign banks tightened standards for below-investment-grade firms, indicating selective risk appetite.
- Relative to pre-pandemic, standards for some consumer categories remain tighter, suggesting lingering caution even as underwriting normalizes.

Net effect: SLOOS points to improving credit supply that reinforces the FOMC’s accommodative stance and recovery narrative, but with uneven easing across risk tiers. Relative to the FSR-tempered view, this nudges the tone modestly more positive while remaining risk-aware.
